Existing system limits
Limit category
Limit
Workflow execution limit
If a workflow run reaches this limit, the workflow run is cancelled. This period includes execution duration, and time spent on waiting and approval.
Workflow execution limit
Workflow execution limit
A job matrix can generate a maximum of 256 jobs per workflow run. This limit applies to both GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners.
Workflow execution limit
A workflow run can be re-run a maximum of 50 times. This limit includes both full re-runs and re-runs of a subset of jobs.

A check suite can have a maximum of 50,000 check runs. This limit applies to check runs created through the Checks API and by GitHub Actions workflow runs. When a check suite reaches this limit, additional check runs cannot be created for that check suite.
Workflow trigger event rate limit
Each repository is limited to events triggering a workflow run.

When the limit is reached, the workflow runs that were supposed to be triggered by the webhook events will be blocked and will not be queued. Reusable workflows are viewed as a single entity. For example, a run with 30 reusable workflows counts as 1 in this instance.
section, up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be queued per concurrency group. Runs beyond this limit will be rejected.
Each job in a workflow can run for up to 5 days of execution time. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails.
Job concurrency limits for GitHub-hosted runners
Each job in a workflow can run for up to 6 hours of execution time. If a job reaches this limit, the job is terminated and fails.

Uploads per minute
200 per minute
Each repository is limited to 200 cache entry uploads per minute. If this limit is exceeded, subsequent cache upload attempts will fail until the rate limit resets.
Downloads per minute
1500 per minute
Each repository is limited to 1500 cache entry downloads per minute. If this limit is exceeded, subsequent cache download attempts will fail until the rate limit resets.
Deletes per minute
400 per minute

Each repository is limited to 400 cache delete operations per minute. If this limit is exceeded, subsequent cache delete attempts will fail until the rate limit resets. Each request to delete caches either by key or by ID counts towards this limit.

GitHub Actions billing
Understand which runner and storage costs your plan covers, how usage measured in different units draws from the included compute usage, and when additional charges apply.
How storage billing works

. Each product measures usage in its own units and applies its own rate. GitHub calculates the cost of that usage, which counts against the included compute usage. After the included amount is consumed, additional usage is billed to your account. The included amount resets at the start of each billi
, where available, when the billing account uses GitHub Team or GitHub Enterprise Cloud.

The calculated cost of eligible runner usage draws from your monthly included compute usage. This value is also available for cloud sandbox compute and memory. Usage is charged to the repository owner, not the person who triggered the workflow runs.

Artifact and cache storage have separate allowances. Storage charges accumulate throughout the month based on hourly usage, and your accrued storage charges reset to zero at the start of each billing cycle.
How storage billing works
GitHub Actions storage billing operates on an
Continuous billing:
Storage charges accrue every hour based on your actual usage throughout the month
The free storage allowance for your plan (for example, 50 GB on the Enterprise plan) is converted to an hourly rate for billing calculations
GitHub Packages billing
The cumulative total of storage used throughout the billing cycle (determines your bill)
Future hourly charges stop accumulating
Storage already accrued during the current billing cycle remains in your total and will appear on your bill
Example (30-day billing cycle):
Days 1-10: Accruing 240 GB-Hours per day (10 GB × 24 hours)
Deleting artifacts reduces your current storage and prevents future charges, but does not remove charges already recorded for the time the storage existed.
Billing calculations use GB-Hours:

Cache storage usage is measured by the peak usage for each hour. The included allowance is 10 GB per repository. For a given hour, if a repository has a peak cache usage of 15 GB, then the repository owner will be charged for the 5 GB of usage above the 10 GB included for that repository. The reposi
The following included compute usage and storage amounts are included in your GitHub plan. The included compute usage resets at the start of each billing cycle.

The included compute usage is expressed as a monetary amount, not a fixed number of minutes or other usage units. Products measure usage in different units, such as minutes, seconds, or GiB-seconds, and apply the corresponding rate. GitHub deducts the calculated cost from the same included compute u

Where larger runners are available, their cost can draw from the included compute usage for billing accounts on GitHub Team and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. Larger runners are billed for public repositories.

GitHub updates your artifact storage usage within 6 to 12 hours. Deleting artifacts frees up space for current storage, but does not reduce your accrued storage usage, which is used to calculate your storage billing for the current billing cycle.
For cached storage, billing charts and reports show only the cost of usage beyond the included 10 GB. At the end of the month, the Actions Cache Storage SKU would show a use of 1008 GB-Hours.
